epic.title: Local Agent State Integration
epic.objective: Establish a secure, provider-neutral, local event pipeline and use a deterministic local simulator to drive the existing three-agent virtual office. This makes the Connector-to-desktop architecture observable and testable before introducing a real provider.
design: A development-only, separate-process simulator drives Ari, Mina, and Sol through a scripted sequence once, then remains connected without further scripted events.

Electron main owns an authenticated Node net listener bound only to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-assigned port; this minimum transport, authentication, runtime validation, synchronization, and reconnection slice moves from the previously deferred EP-04 work into EP-03. Real-provider adapters and production Connector orchestration remain in EP-04.
Main enforces runtime validation, message limits, bounded deduplication, and explicit current-state synchronization before forwarding accepted events.
A narrow preload bridge delivers accepted events and connection status to one in-memory renderer state owner.
React inspection and the existing Phaser presentation consume that state. A simulation-only presentation mapping handles coffee-break animation without changing provider-neutral lifecycle states.
Startup, disconnect, reconnect, renderer reload or remount, and cleanup have explicit behavior. Disconnect retains last-known agent data and displays Disconnected.
Automated and integrated verification covers the full local event path.
exit_criteria: A dedicated development command runs a deterministic three-agent simulator as a separate local Connector process. Its events reach the desktop through the authenticated loopback transport.

Electron main rejects unauthenticated, malformed, unsupported, oversized, duplicate, and otherwise invalid input before it reaches the renderer. Accepted events follow documented identity and arrival-order rules.
The renderer initializes through explicit current-state synchronization and maintains a single in-memory source of truth for agent state, activity, and connection status.
Accepted events update the appropriate existing office presentation and inspection details without recreating Phaser or losing selection.

Startup, Connector loss, reconnection, renderer reload/remount, and application shutdown have documented behavior. Disconnect retains last-known agent data and displays Disconnected without duplicate subscriptions or leaked owned resources.

Automated tests cover the relevant contract, validation, transport, reducer, presentation, synchronization, and lifecycle boundaries. Integrated verification documents visual and interaction behavior and limitations.
Typecheck, lint, tests, and build pass on the final integrated revision. Independent review confirms all approved exit criteria before the maintainer closes the epic.
out_of_scope: Real Codex or other provider adapters
starting or controlling real AI agents
remote access or public network listeners
persistent event history, database, and cross-restart replay
new rooms, artwork, agent movement, or simulation UI controls
production process orchestration, packaging, and general-purpose messaging infrastructure

stories.title: Establish the Local Transport and Trust Boundary
stories.user_story: Define and implement the minimum authenticated local Connector-to-Electron transport, provider-neutral contract changes, ingress validation, and synchronization protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture documentation explicitly assigns the minimum local transport, authentication, runtime validation, synchronization, and reconnection slice to EP-03 and clarifies what remains in EP-04.
Electron main owns a Node net listener bound only to 127.0.0.1 on an OS-assigned port. A session-specific token is required before events are accepted. Endpoint and token are not logged.
The protocol defines a versioned handshake, one framing format, a documented maximum frame size, connection ownership, and rejection/closure behavior. Limits are tested.
Main validates complete supported runtime event payloads, including identity, lifecycle state, bounded activity, source identity, event ID, and timestamp.
Main implements bounded deduplication by (source.instanceId, event.id) and forwards accepted events in arrival order.
Unknown agent IDs are rejected for the fixed three-agent MVP.

The provider-neutral lifecycle vocabulary is preserved; activity is included atomically in state-change events. A separate, explicit simulation-presentation mapping handles the coffee-break animation without equating generic waiting or idle with a coffee break.
An explicit current-state synchronization protocol specifies snapshot schema, snapshot/event ordering, and renderer reload behavior. The transport supports the required messages.
Tests cover successful authentication/delivery and rejection of invalid tokens, malformed or oversized frames, invalid payloads, duplicate events, and clean shutdown.
Existing Electron context isolation, sandboxing, and disabled Node integration remain intact.
stories.boundary: Transport, contracts, validation, and architecture documentation only. No React store, Phaser integration, or scripted simulator sequence.

stories.title: Add the Preload Bridge and In-Memory Agent Store
stories.user_story: Deliver validated events, current-state synchronization, and connection status to one in-memory renderer state owner.
acceptance_criteria: Preload exposes narrow application-specific event, snapshot, and status access without exposing raw ipcRenderer, arbitrary channels, sockets, filesystem access, or generic Node APIs.
A newly loaded renderer can obtain current state without missing subsequent events.
One in-memory renderer store owns the three agents' current lifecycle states and activities, plus connection status.
A pure reducer applies accepted events in arrival order, updates only the intended agent, and follows the approved snapshot protocol.
Duplicate or stale delivery across synchronization boundaries cannot silently roll back current state.
Disconnect retains last-known agent state and activity; connection status remains separate from lifecycle state.
React Strict Mode remount and cleanup do not accumulate listeners or subscriptions.
Tests cover initialization, updates, status changes, snapshot/event ordering, cleanup, and unknown-agent handling.
stories.boundary: Bridge and store only; no Phaser or inspection redesign.

stories.title: Add the Deterministic Local Connector Simulator
stories.user_story: Provide a repeatable, development-only three-agent event source through the real approved transport.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated development command starts the desktop and exactly one simulator process. Existing npm run dev behavior remains unchanged.
Electron main owns the simulator child process in simulation mode and passes the endpoint and session token through a controlled environment without printing the token.
The simulator completes authentication and synchronization before sending live events.
It uses the existing Ari, Mina, and Sol IDs and publishes a documented initial snapshot and fixed transition sequence.
Repeated runs preserve transition order, event-ID sequence, state/activity payloads, and controlled delays. Each new process uses a fresh source.instanceId.
All three agents visibly change state or activity over the sequence, including Sol's explicit simulation-only coffee-break presentation.
The sequence runs once and stops producing scripted events while the Connector remains connected.
Stopping the simulator clears timers and closes its socket. Desktop shutdown terminates its owned simulator process.
Controlled-time tests verify sequencing, event shape, identity rules, and cleanup.
No real providers are invoked and no provider credentials are read.
stories.boundary: Simulator and development command only; no UI controls or real-provider adapter.

stories.title: Drive the Virtual Office from Agent State
stories.user_story: Replace mutable mock-fixture state with renderer-store state while retaining existing visual metadata and interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Agent state and activity in the office come from the renderer store, not fixed mock-fixture runtime values.
Existing fixtures may retain stable identity, sprite, anchor, and approved visual metadata.
Accepted events update only the corresponding agent's inspection details and mapped Phaser presentation.
Selection persists through state/activity updates; events for other agents do not replace selection.
Ordinary state changes do not recreate the Phaser game or room; sprites update through a narrow presentation interface.
The existing room, three agent identities, anchors, 640x360 canvas, selection, and window-size behavior remain intact.
The UI clearly identifies its data as a local simulation rather than live provider activity.
Tests cover presentation mapping, sprite updates, and inspection/selection consistency.
stories.boundary: Existing office presentation and inspection only; no visual redesign or new agents.

stories.title: Complete Connection Loss and Resynchronization Behavior
stories.user_story: Show Connector availability accurately, retain last-known agent data during interruptions, and safely resume after reconnection.
acceptance_criteria: The UI distinguishes connecting, connected, and disconnected from agent lifecycle states.
Startup without a Connector follows a documented failure/timeout policy and eventually displays Disconnected.
Connector loss displays Disconnected while preserving last-known agent states and activities.
Reconnection establishes a new authenticated session and completes current-state synchronization before normal updates resume.
Stale events from an earlier session cannot overwrite the active session's synchronized state.
Renderer reload/remount restores current state and status without missing or duplicating updates.
Simulator restart does not accumulate processes, sockets, timers, IPC listeners, React subscriptions, or Phaser canvases.
Desktop shutdown releases its owned listener and simulator process.
Tests cover startup failure, loss, reconnect, stale-session input, reload/remount, and cleanup.
stories.boundary: Local availability and recovery only; no persistent queue or general offline framework.

stories.title: Verify the Integrated Local Event MVP
stories.user_story: Produce exact-revision evidence that the simulated local event pipeline updates the office safely and predictably.
acceptance_criteria: The dedicated simulation command launches the integrated desktop and delivers events through the Connector transport.
Verification demonstrates initial synchronization and scripted transitions for all three agents, including presentation and activity text.
Selection persists and inspection updates while events arrive.
Verification covers startup without a Connector, disconnect with retained state, reconnect/resynchronization, renderer reload/remount, and shutdown.
Representative unauthenticated, invalid, oversized, and duplicate inputs are rejected without unintended renderer changes.
Automated tests cover relevant deterministic and integration boundaries without unnecessary duplication.
A committed verification report documents event flow, security/protocol checks, visual and accessibility observations, lifecycle checks, evidence provenance, and limitations.
Typecheck, lint, tests, and build pass on the final integrated revision.
Independent review confirms every approved EP-03 exit criterion before maintainer approval.
stories.boundary: Verification and narrowly necessary fixes only; no new features.
